why: In next/, ticket 1153 changes only the Node quota fixture. A scoped one-entry cache reuses admission services within one World and limits generation. Every input still sends. Each limits setter creates an Equal.byReference key, each cache lookup uses a fresh Layer MemoMap, and failures expire immediately. The existing runtime suite, cases, histories, assertions, seed, run counts, limits and timeout are unchanged.
note: Source-extracted wiring ran against installed Effect 4.1.3 with instrumented no-resource Layers. Two forced and eighty generated cases passed, with seed 119120 and forty cases per property, recording 710 setup builds and 824 sends. Scope cleanup and two-World independence passed. Three temporary faults failed their intended checks and were restored. A plain-object key first failed the same-limits setter case; the approved amendment uses reference-only keys. Original failed proof is retained privately. Scoped format and lint, the narrow libfabrika TypeScript compiler, shrinking-list checks, whitespace checks and a one-commit leak check passed. Full compiler and full lint are not credited. No local SQL/resource law, Linux suite, workflow dispatch, benchmark or speed study ran. Pure proof supplies no SQL, reopen or replay execution evidence. The recorded start is the first observed shell setup timestamp; usage and cost remain unknown.
